(By Sri. T.Kodandarama,
 Advocate.)
 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- for the death of one Venkataravanappa in a road traffic accident dated 16.10.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, On 16.10.2022 at about 2.45pm the deceased Venkataravanappa was riding CT-100 Two Wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HA-6911 on the extreme left side of SH-33 Road, i.e., from Koratagere towards Tumkur side slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

While so proceeding, when he reached Opposite to Matha Annapoorneshwari Petrol Bunk, near Jatti Agrahara, Koratagere, Tumkur, a Lorry bearing Reg.No.TS-07-UF-4985 suddenly came in a reverse Gear in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the deceased's motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to impact he fell down along with the Two wheeler and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, immediately deceased was shifted to Koratagere Govt.
Hospital, wherein Post Mortem was conducted and the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies by spending more than Rs.1,00,000/-.

Prior to the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy, working as a Cashier at Naveen Comfort Bar and Restaurant and earning a sum of Rs.45,000/- per month and contributing entire amount to the family.
Due to sudden demise of the deceased, the petitioners are facing great hardship, mental shock and agony.
The petitioners have lost earning member of the family, resulting in great financial loss.

The accident was caused due to the rash and negligent Kalpana vs Mohammad Iliyas on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65102247/
2 driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TS-07-UF-4985.
The Jurisdictional Koratagere Police have registered a case against the driver of the said Lorry in Cr.No.256/2022.
The 1st respondent being the Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the said Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels.
But the respondent No.2 alone filed written statement.

5. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
It has denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the 1 st respondent in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TS-07-UF-4985 and the policy was in existence as on the date of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the Lorry in the accident but, the accident is purely self accident by the deceased.
There is a non-joinder of necessary parties to the petition.
The driver of the offending Lorry did not have a valid DL as on the date of accident.
There is non-compliance of Sec.158(6) and 134(c) of MV Act

Further it has denied the age,
income and avocation of the deceased and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Venkataravanappa?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Venkataravanappa had died due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 16.10.2022 at about 2.45am opposite to Matha Annapurneshwari Petrol Bunk, Near Jatti Agrahara, Koratagere, Tumkur, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TS-07-UF-4985 as alleged?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
4.

What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined 1st petitioner/Wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 15.
They have also got examined MR.Pradeepkumar K.R. - Administrator and Manager of the Naveen Comforts as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.16 to 18.
On the other side the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any document.

8. Heard both Counsels and perused the materials on record.
Kalpana vs Mohammad Iliyas on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65102247/
3

The counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the following decision:
MFA No.104099/2017 9.

My finding to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the affirmative  Issue Nos.2 & 3: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  Following:
 REASONS  10. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and has reiterated about the relationship in her affidavit in chief.
In addition she got marked Notarized copy of Aadhar cards of the deceased and the petitioners as per Ex.P.10 and also got marked Ration Card of the family at Ex.P.11.
According to Ex.P.10 in the Aadhar Card of the deceased his father's name is shown as Venkateshappa who is the petitioner No.4.
In the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.1 her Husband's name is shown as Venkataravanappa and in the Aadhar Cards of the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 their father's name is shown as Venkataravanappa.
In the Aadhar Card of the Petitioner No.5 her husband's name is shown as Venkateshappa who is the petitioner No.4 and father of the deceased.
In the Aadhar Card of the Petitioner No.4 his father's name is shown as Venkataravanappa.
In the same manner, in the Ration Card all the Petitioners name and the deceased name is also mentioned as the family members.
In Ex.P.3 Inquest Mahazar deceased's father name is shown as Venkateshappa who is the petitioner No.4.
Therefore, the Tribunal holds that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the children and Petitioner Nos.4 & 5 are the father and mother of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-

The counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the following decision:
MFA No.104099/2017
Wherein
the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that the standard of proof required in proving the accident is that of preponderance of possibility.
In cases of accident getting an eye witness is difficult and formal proof in the form of police records would be sufficient.

The Petitioners, to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry has examined First Petitioner/Wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 9.
During the cross examination of PW.1, stated that the accident spot is main Road.
The front portion of the bike is damaged.
The deceased was going alone in the bike.

Kalpana vs Mohammad Iliyas on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65102247/
4 12.
The police have filed charge sheet after thorough investigation at Ex.P.1 against the driver of the offending Lorry bearing No.TX-07-UF-4985.
The FIR was registered on the same day of accident on the complaint of wife of the deceased at Ex.P.2.
The inquest mahazar at Ex.
P.3 The spot mahazar at Ex.P.4 shows the police investigation done on the spot of the accident.
Ex. P.5
spot sketch shows the spot of the accident is the footpath with sketch.
Ex . P.6
seizure mahazar gives the details of the vehicles involved in the accident, which are seized by the police after investigation.
Ex . P.7
PM report shows that the death of the deceased is due to hypovolamic Shock and cardio respiratory arrest due to head injury as a resulting in RTA.
Ex.P.8 is the notice issued to the RC owner from the police and reply to the notice.
Ex . P.9

IMV report shows that the offending vehicle Lorry bearing bearing No.TS-07-UF-4985 got damaged to its rear right side tail lamp grill dent and damaged and deceased's motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HA-6911 also got damaged to its front handle bar twisted,
front head light assembly, front both forks, front crash guard and rear tail lamp assembly damaged.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents.

Therefore, on the basis of the documents on records and relying on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the decision stated supra, this Tribunal holds that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TS-07-UF-4985.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No. 3:-
The petitioners averred that the deceased was a Cashier at Naveen Comfort Bar and Restaurant and earning sum of Rs.45,000/- per month.
In this regard the petitioners have produced original employee certificate of the deceased and salary slip of the deceased as per Exs.P.14 & 15.

In this regard the petitioners have also got examined Mr.Pradeepkumar K.R. - Administrator/Manager of the Naveen Comforts Bar and Restaurant as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.16 to 18 authorization letter, notarized copy of Bar license and notarized copy of Aadhar Card.

During his cross examination,
he has admitted that they were not taking any voucher from the employee while giving the salary and there is no appointment letter while taking in the employees.
The Ex.P.15 Salary slip issued by the employer to the deceased does not bear the year and month.
Further admitted that the salary was credited to the employees account.

But the petitioners or the PW.2 did not produce Bank Statement, attendance register,
Acquittance register etc., to show the salary details of the deceased.
The Noukarnama at Ex.P.14 makes it clear that the deceased was working in the Bar, but the salary slip at Ex.P.15 does not inspire confidence of the court.
On overall perusal of the documents produced by Pws.1 & 2 and cross examination of PW.2, and since the accident occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,500/- per month.
Age of the deceased 14.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.10.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.

As per the said document, the date of birth of the deceased was 05.05.1985 and the accident occurred Kalpana vs Mohammad Iliyas on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65102247/
5 on 16.10.2020.
As such, the age of the deceased is 37 years as on the date of accident.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased comes below 40 years age slab, 40% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
Therefore, Rs.6,200/- future prospectus is to be added to his monthly income, then it comes to Rs.21,700/-.
As per Principles laid down in the case of Sarala Verma the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 15.
The deceased has a wife, 2 minor children and Father and Mother.
They are all dependents of the deceased.
Since there are Five dependents then 1/4th of the income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.16,275/- (Rs.21,700/- - Rs.5,425/-).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.29,29,500/- (Rs.16,275/- X 12 x 15 = Rs.29,29,500/-).

ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to her family.

With respect to a spouse,
it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".
15.

This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
16.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 28 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.

Similarly, the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased, they have lost their loving, care taking father and petitioner Nos.4 & 5 Father and Mother of the deceased, they have also lost their loving and care taking son in the old age of 65 and 64 years respectively.
Therefore, they are also entitled to Rs.44,000/- each, in total Rs.2,20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.

iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:-
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation and funeral expenses and obsequies etc.
In this regard the petitioners have not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.

Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.

Kalpana vs Mohammad Iliyas on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65102247/
6 iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:-
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.15,500/- per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/4th of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.31,89,500/-.
LIABILITY 17.
The respondents have failed to prove their defence by leading evidence.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 & 2 being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the Petitioners and satisfy the award.
Though the Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.60,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.31,89,500/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 is in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.4:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.31,89,500/- (Rupees Thirty One Lakhs Eighty Nine Thousand and Five Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the in- surer is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.10,00,000/- each shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner Nos.2 & 3 in any Bank of their choice till they attain the age of majority and Rs.2,00,000/- each shall be released to the petitioner Nos.4 & 5 and the remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

Though the Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.60,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.31,89,500/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 is in the affirmative.

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.31,89,500/- (Rupees Thirty One Lakhs Eighty Nine Thousand and Five Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the in- surer is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.10,00,000/- each shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner Nos.2 & 3 in any Bank of their choice till they attain the age of majority and Rs.2,00,000/- each shall be released to the petitioner Nos.4 & 5 and the remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
